FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1, and the repair is verified against the records the task named rather than assumed. The instructions open: 'File the verified SCA-C906 petition with the clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction — the circuit court in which the convictions occurred', adding that where the convictions were had in more than one county the petition groups the information by circuit court and the prosecuting attorney of every county of conviction is served, and add that the petition may not be filed until the page-3 verification has been sworn before a notary and the page-4 certificate of service is complete. I checked that against the two records the packet itself cites. The committed track registry's wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors destination reads: name 'Clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction', detail 'File the verified petition with the circuit clerk…', venue 'The circuit court in which the convictions occurred. Where convictions were had in more than one county, the petition identifies and groups the information by circuit court under the § 61-11-26(d) proviso.' The committed route census carries the identical destination block on this exact route key. The packet-set manifest's file entry agrees. Notarisation is in the manifest too ('Required. The SCA-C906 verification on page 3 is sworn to or affirmed before a notary public or other official'). MASTER_QUEUE still records this obligation as FAILED with the finding 'the packet does not name the office it is filed with' and 'participant-instructions.md has no filing section'; that record is stale on the bytes at this base.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 with A2, and it passes on the first met limb — the packet states the amount, sourced — with the waiver honestly refused and a named checkable authority standing in. I confirmed the figures against the records the route census names, as the task asked. THE $200: the packet says 'The circuit clerk charges the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee, which the official text sets at $200.' The committed track registry's wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors destination.detail says 'paying the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee of $200', the committed route census carries the same sentence on this route key, and the committed packet-set manifest's pay_fee entry says the same. THE $100: 'A person who obtains an order of expungement pays $100 to the records division of the West Virginia State Police under § 61-11-26(n)', which the same three records carry and which the compiled state profile independently corroborates. THE COMPILED PROFILE, checked because the task said the repair deliberately did not draw the number from it: src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WV-west-virginia.json is named as a requiredSourceId for this route and its only fee sentence is 'For 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the circuit clerk charges the same fee as filing a civil action, and a person who receives an expungement order must pay a $100 West Virginia State Police processing fee.' The string '59-1-11' does not occur in that file at all and $100 is the only dollar figure in it. So the profile is silent on the number rather than in conflict with it, and the $200 comes from two other held records that do state it. THE WAIVER: the packet says 'No held source establishes a waiver route for this filing', explains that the $100 is waived only on a § 61-11-26a petition which is a different route, declines to name a form or to tell the participant they qualify, and names the office to ask — 'the clerk of the circuit court of the county of conviction, the same office you file with'. The manifest's apply_fee_waiver entry says exactly that: 'none under § 61-11-26. The $100 State Police fee is waived only on a § 61-11-26a petition. Any relief from the $200 circuit clerk fee would be under the circuit court's ordinary civil indigency practice, which the controlling review did not establish.' That is the determination's third met branch, done properly and with the authority in the same paragraph as the refusal. CUSTODY NOTE, not a failure: no held BYTES in this container carry § 59-1-11 itself — the $200 lives inside two committed LegalEase-authored records that assert 'the official text sets at $200' and cite source-url https://code.wvlegislature.gov/59-1-11/, which the repository does not hold. Under A2 those committed records ARE the repository, so stating the figure is the correct behaviour; but the figure's freshness rests on a source-acquisition gap rather than on held bytes, and a Captain should know that before promotion. APPLIED A3, WHICH POSTDATES THIS ROW'S BASE AND WHICH I READ FROM THE CAPTAIN HEAD. A3 holds that a record establishes an answer only for the route it actually addresses, and that a line keyed to a different statutory section is a sibling-route inference A2 already forbids. Run on this route's fee fact — the circuit clerk's charge for a § 61-11-26 misdemeanour conviction expungement petition — the test comes out clean, and it shows the repair dodged a live trap of exactly A3's shape. THE RECORDS THAT DO ADDRESS THIS ROUTE: the track registry entry is keyed by trackId to this track, the route census entry is keyed by the full route key, and the packet-set manifest entry is keyed by packetSetId; all three carry the § 59-1-11(a)(1) $200 sentence for this route and nothing else. THE PROFILE, READ PER FACT RATHER THAN PER DOCUMENT: its § 61-11-26 line does address this route's statute, and what it establishes is the $100 State Police fee plus a cross-reference to the civil-action fee with no number — silence on the figure, not a different route's figure. THE TRAP IT AVOIDED: the same compiled profile also carries, three times over, 'For 61-11-25 acquittal/dismissal/diversion/deferred-adjudication expungement, no filing fees or costs are charged' and 'Fee rule: no filing fees or costs are charged for a 61-11-25 action.' Section 61-11-25 is not § 61-11-26. A repairer treating the profile as one held document — which A2 read literally licensed — could have published 'no filing fee' for a petition that in fact costs $200, and the participant would have arrived at the circuit clerk's counter with nothing. That is the California 1203.4 trap with the sign flipped and the stakes higher, and the repair did not walk into it. A3 confirms the sourcing choice the task described was not merely defensible but required.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the recipients, the method and the timing, sourced, and marks the one recipient the participant must NOT serve. It names the five § 61-11-26(e) recipients in a numbered list — the Superintendent of the West Virginia State Police; the prosecuting attorney of the county or counties of conviction; the chief law-enforcement officer of the arresting agency; the superintendent, warden or Commissioner of Corrections of any institution of confinement; and the circuit, magistrate or municipal court that disposed of the charge — and then states the § 61-11-26(f) carve-out in bold: 'Identified victims are served by the prosecuting attorney, not by you. Do not serve a victim yourself.' It closes with the timing rule, that the page-4 certificate is completed only after service has actually happened. Checked against the records: the track registry destination.detail says 'Serve the five § 61-11-26(e) recipients and file the completed certificate of service. The prosecuting attorney, not the petitioner, serves identified victims'; the route census carries the same; the packet-set manifest's serve_party entry says the same and adds, under S.B. 562, the prosecuting attorney of every county of conviction where expungement is sought — which this family's instructions do carry, in its filing section. The manifest also warns that the Utah-style general service-of-process page 'must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have', and the packet imports none of that.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet draws its boundary and carries no approval. 'This is a prepared set of official West Virginia forms built for review. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the circuit court will grant expungement.' It names what it will not complete — 'The participant signature, signature date, verification/notary completion, and the entire certificate of service remain blank and protected' — and it refuses to invent the participant's own sworn content, listing grounds for expungement and rehabilitation history as things to 'supply your own truthful' answers for. openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.asked: Whether relief under W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b (and § 60A-4-407) counts against the once-per-lifetime limit in § 61-11-26(o).
openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.whereItLives: data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, on the shared node wv_common_conv_procedure — 'Shared Conviction Expungement Procedure, Exclusion Screen and Once-Per-Lifetime Bundling Node' — which is the node this family's own exclusions defer to for the fifteen § 61-11-26(c) subdivisions. Its text: 'Section 61-11-26(o) by its terms reaches only §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a, and neither § 60A-4-407 nor § 17C-5-2b cross-references it; both were read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and neither contains a limit referring to § 61-11-26. The textual reading is therefore that they are separate limits in separate statutes, but a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime petition needs a settled answer rather than a textual reading.'
openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.isItAnExclusionForThisFamily: Yes. This family's own exclusions in the track registry list 'A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once', and the route census's statuteOrAuthority for this exact route key names W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(o) explicitly.
openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.doesThePacketAddressIt: NO. I searched the whole of participant-instructions.md: it contains no mention of the once-per-lifetime limit, no mention of § 61-11-26(o), no mention of § 17C-5-2b and no mention of § 60A-4-407. A participant is told what to file, where, what it costs and whom to serve, and is not told that filing spends a remedy they get once.
openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.whatIDidWithThat: Recorded, as instructed, and not answered. I did not score it as an obligation failure: it is an open legal question plus a disclosure gap that sits outside the fifteen, and MASTER_QUEUE carries legalInputStatus SETTLED with no lane hold for this family. It is put to the Captain below.
openCounselQuestionRecordedNotAnswered.secondOpenQuestionOnTheSameNode: The same node also carries an unanswered venue question — whether a county-of-residence venue option exists for a multi-county petition — which bears directly on wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors-set. The packet takes the county-of-conviction reading, which is what the route census's own runtime-authority-decision note settles ('No residence-county venue: subsections (a)(1) and (a)(2) both direct the petition to the circuit court in which the conviction occurred'), so the packet follows the settled reading rather than the open one.

openQuestionsForTheCaptain: Neither West Virginia packet tells the participant that § 61-11-26 relief is once per lifetime, though the once-only bar is a listed exclusion on both tracks and § 61-11-26(o) is named in each route's statuteOrAuthority. Whether that disclosure belongs in the packet is a counsel call, not a verifier call, but a participant choosing to spend a once-per-lifetime remedy on a single misdemeanour ought to be told that is what they are doing.
The $200 figure is held only as an assertion inside committed LegalEase records citing an unheld source-url. A source-acquisition lane should acquire § 59-1-11 itself before this route is promoted.
